# convex_default_environment_variable (Resource)

Manages one default environment variable for a Convex project.

~> **Defaults apply only to deployments created afterwards.** Convex uses these values when a new deployment is created and does not push them to deployments that already exist, nor keep them in sync. Changing one here has no effect on a running deployment.

Each resource manages a single `(name, deployment_type)` pair, which is exactly how the API keys these variables. Variables that Terraform does not declare are left alone.

The API only upserts, so it cannot tell a create from an update. Creating a variable that already exists therefore fails rather than silently overwriting a value set elsewhere; import it instead -- the error reports the import command.

Writes are retried on transient 5xx failures, which Convex has been seen returning when several variables of one project are written at once. If it persists, `terraform apply -parallelism=1` serialises them.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "convex_project" "app" {
  team_id = var.convex_team_id
  name    = "My Application"
}

# The same name can carry a different value per deployment type, so each pair
# is its own resource.
resource "convex_default_environment_variable" "sentry_prod" {
  project_id      = convex_project.app.id
  deployment_type = "prod"
  name            = "SENTRY_DSN"
  value           = var.sentry_dsn_prod
}

resource "convex_default_environment_variable" "sentry_dev" {
  project_id      = convex_project.app.id
  deployment_type = "dev"
  name            = "SENTRY_DSN"
  value           = var.sentry_dsn_dev
}

# Spanning several types is a for_each over the types you want.
resource "convex_default_environment_variable" "log_level" {
  for_each = toset(["dev", "preview"])

  project_id      = convex_project.app.id
  deployment_type = each.key
  name            = "LOG_LEVEL"
  value           = "debug"
}

# Defaults apply when a deployment is created, so declare them before the
# deployment that should pick them up.
resource "convex_deployment" "prod" {
  project_id      = convex_project.app.id
  deployment_type = "prod"
  is_default      = true

  depends_on = [convex_default_environment_variable.sentry_prod]
}

variable "sentry_dsn_prod" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "sentry_dsn_dev" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `deployment_type` (String) Deployment type the default applies to: `dev`, `prod`, `preview` or `custom`. The same variable name can carry a different value per type, so this is part of the resource's identity. Changing it forces a new resource.
- `name` (String) Name of the environment variable, for example `SENTRY_DSN`. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `project_id` (Number) Numeric identifier of the project. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `value` (String, Sensitive) Value of the environment variable. Marked sensitive, since these commonly hold credentials; note that the value is stored in Terraform state either way. Can be changed in place.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Default environment variables are imported as
# "<project_id>/<deployment_type>/<name>". Only the first two separators are
# significant, so a name containing "/" survives.
terraform import convex_default_environment_variable.sentry_prod 12345/prod/SENTRY_DSN
```
